     2	
     3	This ledger maps labels of the manuscript on the second moment of the
     4	Stratonovich hyperbolic Anderson model with Gaussian noise fractional in time
     5	to the Lean declarations in this package. Labels and TeX line numbers refer to
     6	the manuscript revision a284420, and labels are written exactly as in its
     7	LaTeX source (for example `P:clock-copy-obstruction`). The ledger was written
     8	and reviewed at the earlier revisions cf979d6, 669ccc9, ba01d98, 3920258 and
     9	975feb3. Revision a284420 makes two mathematical edits that the ledger
    10	follows. (1) In `notes/integrated_spatial_occupation.tex` it adds Lemma
    11	`L:spatial-fourier-bound` (lines 101-164, display `E:spatial-fourier-bound`),
    12	the deterministic bound `A_sp(g) <= 2^(1+alpha) R_alpha b^(alpha/2)` that
    13	`SpatialFourierBound` already proved, and the proof of
    14	`P:spatial-smooth-ratio` (same label and statement) now derives `R_0 < inf`
    15	from it, independently of the finiteness of `S_1^pos`, which it keeps only
    16	for the score inequality. (2) In the main file, `L:damped-homogeneous-norms`
    17	replaces its smoothing and truncation sentence by the multiplier comparison
    18	`E:damped-multiplier-comparison` (a measurable multiplier `m` in `[0,1]`,
    19	nested measurable Laplace domains, positivity after time integration,
    20	scaling asserted only for the original covariance) and its proof by the
    21	corresponding argument. The other changes since 975feb3 are prose and front
    22	matter (title, abstract, preface, a theory-outlook chapter, the reader
    23	edition, Appendices F and G, the list of notation moved to the back).
    24	Every cited label exists exactly once at a284420. Three of them are new at
    25	a284420 and do not exist at 975feb3: `L:spatial-fourier-bound`,
    26	`E:spatial-fourier-bound` and `E:damped-multiplier-comparison`. Every other

    30	`P:spatial-smooth-ratio` (proof only), `L:damped-homogeneous-norms`

    38	
    39	- The "What it states" column is a faithful paraphrase, sometimes
    40	  shortened. The exact statement is the Lean type in
    41	  `StratonovichHAMAudit/<Module>.lean` (step modules) or
    42	  `StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/<Module>.lean` (library modules: whole results, narrower results, foundations and proof steps);
    43	  `Audit/<module>/` prints the elaborated types.
    44	- The rows cover every public theorem (2050) and 418 definitions whose
    45	  values are stated as facts or that name a manuscript object. The other 89
    46	  public definitions have no rows of their own: 85 (for example `kappa`,
    47	  `delta`, `gauge`, `counts`, `InventoryProduct.partialEval`,

    55	  steps only: exact identities, polynomial and rational certificates,
    56	  real-power bookkeeping, parameter ranges, and a few finite-dimensional

    59	  `FockForm` and so formalizes the special case of `L:finite-word-cutoff`
    60	  with one Gaussian coordinate per color (section "HermiteWordFock (narrower result: `L:finite-word-cutoff` for one Gaussian mode per color and single finite words; finite sums and Bochner integrals not formalized)"); the
    61	  multi-mode case is not formalized.
    62	- Section headings use three categories. (A) "whole result": every
    63	  conclusion of the labelled result is a Lean conclusion under the
    64	  manuscript's hypotheses, possibly with named supplied inputs that are
    65	  disclosed (coverage class same-assumptions or inputs-supplied, conclusion
    66	  full); no other section carries it. (B) "narrower result: ...": a labelled
    67	  result some of whose conclusions are not Lean conclusions, or are proved
    68	  for a modelled object (the class `O` by joint representatives, the rate in
    69	  Rayleigh form, the cost in integral form, an abstract structure standing
    70	  for an object the manuscript constructs, an object that is not constructed)
    71	  whose identification with the manuscript's object is not formalized; the
    72	  heading names what is missing. The one exception is a registered model
    73	  choice (next item): a result whose only modelled object is such a choice
    74	  stays a whole result, and its section names the model.
    75	  Discharging a named input in a completion module does not turn a narrower
    76	  result into a whole one. (C) "foundation: ..." or "proof steps ...": facts
    77	  used by labelled results, not a labelled result themselves; every
    78	  `StratonovichHAMAudit` section except `HermiteWordFock` is of this kind.
    79	  The Index by label is a pointer table: each manuscript label (and one row
    80	  for declarations with no direct label) points to the sections whose tables
    81	  formalize it, each followed by the category phrase of that section's
    82	  heading. It carries no per-declaration lists or qualifiers: what each
    83	  declaration states and the analytic inputs it takes are stated once, in
    84	  the section tables. Labelling convention: every backticked manuscript
    85	  label in a section-table label cell is an assignment and creates an Index
    86	  pointer; a label mentioned only as context goes in the "What it states"
    87	  cell as "(Context: ...)"; a "no direct label" cell contains no manuscript
    88	  label.

     1	\section{Covariance bounds for physically masked wave fields}
     2	\label{S:masked-covariance}
     3	
     4	We establish the covariance estimates needed for the operator construction.
     5	Throughout this section, Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog} holds, $a = \alpha_0$, and
     6	$\Gamma \ne 0$. For zero spatial covariance, the spatial spectral measures and
     7	noise variances vanish; the purely temporal estimates remain valid independently
     8	of $\Gamma$. We use the unitary Fourier transform
     9	\[
    10	  \widehat{f}(\xi) = c_d\int_{\R^d}e^{-i\xi\cdot x}f(x)\ud x,
    11	  \qquad c_d = (2\pi)^{-d/2}.
    12	\]
    13	The spectral convention in Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog} means that, for every
    14	complex Schwartz test $\varphi$,
    15	\begin{equation}\label{E:masked-spectral-convention}
    16	  \int_{\R^d}\varphi(x)\Gamma(\ud x)
    17	  = \int_{\R^d}\left(\int_{\R^d}e^{i\xi\cdot x}
    18	  \varphi(x)\ud x\right)\mu(\ud\xi).
    19	\end{equation}
    20	This is an identity of distribution pairings. We will not interchange two
    21	infinite measures in the associated oscillatory expression.
    22	
    23	A positive tempered Radon measure has polynomial mass growth. Indeed, choose a
    24	nonnegative compact smooth test that is at least one on the unit ball, and apply
    25	a defining Schwartz seminorm bound for the distribution to its dilations. Its
    26	mass on a ball of radius $R \ge 1$ is bounded by a power of $R$. Summation over
    27	dyadic shells then gives integrability of $(1+|x|)^{-N}$ for some $N$, and hence
    28	absolute integrability of every Schwartz test. These facts apply to both
    29	$\Gamma$ and $\mu$. Smooth cutoffs converge in the Schwartz topology, so these
    30	integrals agree with the tempered pairings.
    31	
    32	\subsection{Translated spectral growth and physical masks}
    33	
    34	\begin{proposition}[Translated spectral mass]\label{P:masked-spectral-growth}
    35	  Put
    36	  \[
    37	    M_\Gamma = \int_{\R^d}e^{-|x|^2/4}\Gamma(\ud x),
    38	    \qquad C_\Gamma = \frac{eM_\Gamma}{(2\sqrt{\pi})^d}.
    39	  \]
    40	  Then $0 < M_\Gamma < \infty$, and for $y \in \R^d$ and $r > 0$,
    41	  \begin{align}
    42	    \int_{\R^d}e^{-|\xi-y|^2/r^2}\mu(\ud\xi)
    43	    &= \left(\frac{r}{2\sqrt{\pi}}\right)^d
    44	    \int_{\R^d}e^{-r^2|x|^2/4}e^{-iy\cdot x}\Gamma(\ud x),
    45	    \label{E:masked-gaussian-transform}\\
    46	    0 \le \int_{\R^d}e^{-|\xi-y|^2/r^2}\mu(\ud\xi)
    47	    &\le \frac{r^\alpha M_\Gamma}{(2\sqrt{\pi})^d},
    48	    \qquad \mu(B(y,r)) \le C_\Gamma r^\alpha.
    49	    \label{E:masked-translated-ball}
    50	  \end{align}
    51	  The ball may be open or closed.
    52	\end{proposition}
    53	
    54	\begin{proof}
    55	  Temperedness gives finiteness of $M_\Gamma$. Its positivity follows from
    56	  $\Gamma \ne 0$. To check the Fourier constant, set $J(b) = \int_\R
    57	  e^{-Ax^2}e^{ibx}\ud x$ for $A > 0$. Squaring the real Gaussian integral and
    58	  using polar coordinates gives $J(0) = \sqrt{\pi/A}$. Differentiation and
    59	  integration by parts give $J'(b) = -bJ(b)/(2A)$. Therefore, $J(b) =
    60	  \sqrt{\pi/A}e^{-b^2/(4A)}$. Taking products over the coordinates gives
    61	  \[
    62	    \int_{\R^d}e^{-r^2|x|^2/4}e^{i(\xi-y)\cdot x}\ud x
    63	    = \left(\frac{2\sqrt{\pi}}r\right)^d e^{-|\xi-y|^2/r^2}.
    64	  \]
    65	  Apply~\eqref{E:masked-spectral-convention} to the single Schwartz test
    66	  $e^{-r^2|x|^2/4}e^{-iy\cdot x}$ to obtain \eqref{E:masked-gaussian-transform}.
    67	  Its left side is nonnegative. Taking the absolute value on the right removes
    68	  the complex phase because $\Gamma$ is nonnegative. The pushforward of $\Gamma$
    69	  by $x \mapsto rx$ assigns mass $r^{\alpha-d}\Gamma(A)$ to a Borel set $A$.
    70	  Thus,
    71	  \[
    72	    \int e^{-r^2|x|^2/4}\Gamma(\ud x) = r^{\alpha-d}M_\Gamma.
    73	  \]
    74	  This proves the Gaussian bound. On either ball $B(y,r)$ the integrand
    75	  $e^{-|\xi-y|^2/r^2}$ is at least $e^{-1}$, proving the mass bound. This proves
    76	  Proposition~\ref{P:masked-spectral-growth}.
    77	\end{proof}
    78	
    79	Choose and fix a real nonzero Schwartz function $\zeta$. For $R > 0$ put
    80	$\zeta_R(x) = \zeta(x/R)$, $k_R = \widehat{\zeta_R}$ and $L =
    81	\|\widehat{\zeta}\|_1$. Then $k_R(u) = R^d\widehat{\zeta}(Ru)$ and $\|k_R\|_1 =
    82	L > 0$. Define
    83	\begin{equation}\label{E:masked-auxiliary-measure}
    84	  \nu_R(\ud\eta) = \rho_R(\eta)\ud\eta,
    85	  \qquad \rho_R(\eta) = c_d^2L\int |k_R(\xi-\eta)|\mu(\ud\xi).
    86	\end{equation}
    87	
    88	\begin{proposition}[Auxiliary mask norm]\label{P:masked-auxiliary-norm}
    89	  The measure $\nu_R$ is even, tempered and Radon, with
    90	  \begin{equation}\label{E:masked-auxiliary-growth}
    91	    \nu_R(B(y,r)) \le c_d^2L^2C_\Gamma r^\alpha
    92	  \end{equation}
    93	  for all $y \in \R^d$ and $r > 0$, uniformly in $R > 0$. If $H$ is a separable
    94	  complex Hilbert space and $F$ is an $H$-valued Schwartz function, then
    95	  \begin{equation}\label{E:masked-hilbert-fourier}
    96	    \int \|\widehat{\zeta_RF}(\xi)\|_H^2\mu(\ud\xi)
    97	    \le \int \|\widehat{F}(\eta)\|_H^2\nu_R(\ud\eta).
    98	  \end{equation}
    99	  For a real $H$, the same assertion holds after complexification.
   100	\end{proposition}
   101	
   102	\begin{proof}
   103	  Schwartz decay of $k_R$ and polynomial growth of $\mu$ show that
   104	  $\rho_R(\eta)$ is finite at every $\eta$. On compact sets of $\eta$, the
   105	  integrands have a common integrable bound. Dominated convergence therefore
   106	  makes $\rho_R$ continuous, and $\nu_R$ is Radon. Since $\zeta$ is real,
   107	  $k_R(-u) = \overline{k_R(u)}$. Evenness of $\mu$ gives evenness of $\rho_R$.
   108	  Tonelli's theorem gives
   109	  \[
   110	    \nu_R(B(y,r)) = c_d^2L\int |k_R(u)|\mu(B(y+u,r))\ud u.
   111	  \]
   112	  Proposition~\ref{P:masked-spectral-growth} and $\|k_R\|_1 = L$ give
   113	  \eqref{E:masked-auxiliary-growth}. Polynomial growth on centered balls proves
   114	  temperedness by the same dyadic argument as above.
   115	
   116	  Bochner Fourier integration gives
   117	  \[
   118	    \widehat{\zeta_RF}(\xi)
   119	    = c_d\int k_R(\xi-\eta)\widehat{F}(\eta)\ud\eta.
   120	  \]
   121	  For scalar Schwartz functions this follows by Fourier inversion and absolute
   122	  integrability. It follows next for finite-rank Hilbert-valued functions. For
   123	  general $F$, take projections onto the successive spans of a countable
   124	  orthonormal basis of its separable range closure. They converge pointwise in
   125	  norm. The Schwartz bounds on $F$ dominate the Fourier integrals, proving the
   126	  identity by dominated convergence. In a finite-dimensional space the full
   127	  identity projection suffices; the zero space is immediate. The triangle
   128	  inequality and weighted Cauchy--Schwarz yield
   129	  \[
   130	    \|\widehat{\zeta_RF}(\xi)\|_H^2
   131	    \le c_d^2L\int |k_R(\xi-\eta)|\|\widehat{F}(\eta)\|_H^2\ud\eta.
   132	  \]

   134	  \eqref{E:masked-hilbert-fourier}. Its right side is finite by Schwartz decay
   135	  and temperedness of $\nu_R$. This proves
   136	  Proposition~\ref{P:masked-auxiliary-norm}.
   137	\end{proof}

  2289	  Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space, $A_0$ a bounded nonnegative selfadjoint
  2290	  operator, and $B$ a bounded selfadjoint operator. Write $A_\rho = \rho^2+A_0$.

   281	  \label{P:radius-mean-anchor}
   282	  Fix integer $B \ge 1$ and use the true block partition $B,\delta,N,\ell_m$ of
   283	  Section~\ref{S:actual-cameron-mean}, with $0 < \delta < \min(1,1/B)$ and $N =
   284	  \lfloor1/(\delta B)\rfloor$. For $Y_m$ as in
   285	  Corollary~\ref{C:radius-covariance-residuals}, put
   286	  \[
   287	    X_m(u)=g_\delta M_R(Y_m)(\min(u,\ell_m)),\qquad
   288	    Z_\delta=\left(\delta\sum_{m=0}^N
   289	    \|X_m\|_{C^\theta}^p\right)^{1/p},\qquad
   290	    g_\delta=\delta^{(1-a)/2},
   291	  \]
   292	  for any fixed $p \ge 1$. Then
   293	  \begin{equation}\label{E:radius-mean-anchor}
   294	    \E Z_\delta\le(2/B)^{1/p}C_{Q,B}\sqrt p\,
   295	    g_\delta R^{d/Q}.
   296	  \end{equation}
   297	  In particular, for $R_\delta = \delta^{-1}+2$,
   298	  \begin{equation}\label{E:radius-mean-anchor-decay}
   299	    2\E Z_\delta
   300	    \le2(2/B)^{1/p}C_{Q,B}\sqrt p\,3^{d/Q}
   301	    \delta^{e_{\rm anchor}}\longrightarrow0,\qquad
   302	    e_{\rm anchor}=\frac{1-a}{2}-\frac dQ>0 .
   303	  \end{equation}
   304	  Both bounds are uniform in the deterministic orthogonal projection.
   305	\end{proposition}
   306	
   307	\begin{proof}
   308	  Stopping an interaction primitive starting at zero and extending it constantly
   309	  to $B$ does not increase its supremum or H\"older seminorm. An empty last
   310	  interval gives the zero path. Probability normalization and Lyapunov give
   311	  \begin{align*}
   312	    \E Z_\delta
   313	    &\le(\E Z_\delta^p)^{1/p}
   314	    =\left(\delta\sum_{m=0}^N
   315	    \E\|X_m\|_{C^\theta}^p\right)^{1/p}\\
   316	    &\le[\delta(N+1)]^{1/p}g_\delta
   317	    C_{Q,B}\sqrt p\,R^{d/Q}.
   318	  \end{align*}
   319	  This is linearity for a finite sum; no time-block independence or maximum over
   320	  blocks is used. Since $\delta B < 1$, we have $N \ge 1$ and $N+1 \le 2/(\delta
   321	  B)$, proving~\eqref{E:radius-mean-anchor}.

   323	  Now $R_\delta \le 3/\delta$ because $\delta < 1$. The last condition
   324	  in~\eqref{E:radius-anchor-Q} is equivalent to $Q(1-a) > 2d$. Dividing by $2Q >

   328	  $B,p,Q$ and model, uniformly in every deterministic residual projection. This
   329	  proves Proposition~\ref{P:radius-mean-anchor}.
   330	\end{proof}
